text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

Panel composition alone proves nothing. Women don't systematically favour women on hiring panels — the research is mixed and effects are small. In a profession where women are a minority, an all-women panel is more likely a sign of deliberate optics than of bias against you. Raising it makes you look like someone searching for an explanation other than the decision itself, which damages you internally and legally weakens any real claim.

What's actually substantive: more years and bigger projects don't win a leadership role. "Excellent client relationships" is a business-development qualification, and heads of group sell work.

Chase the written explanation — politely, in writing, copying HR. The silence is the legitimate grievance.
